fieldMarks: Medium, rangy deer standing 91–97 cm at the shoulder
Mature bucks (3–4 years and older) carry broad palmate antlers; younger bucks have simple beams and points
Four colour forms: common (rust with white spots, fading in winter), menil (tan, spots distinct in winter), white (dark eyes) and black
Black line down the back often joins the black upper tail in the common form
behavior: Rut mid-September into November, peaking in October; bucks defend a small 'stand'
After the rut males form bachelor groups while does and young stay separate
Feeds as a grazer or browser depending on competition with livestock and white-tailed deer
habitat: Feeds in open grassy areas but needs tree cover and undergrowth; deciduous or mixed woodland on gently rolling terrain is best.
range: Native to the Mediterranean and Asia Minor. Introduced in North America: Texas has over 10,000 (about a third free-ranging), with other introduced or semi-wild populations in several U.S. states and on western Canadian islands in British Columbia.
